biography.plain_text: John M. Floyd is an American entrepreneur who founded JMFA, a specialist consultancy and software provider for community banks and credit unions. After almost four decades as its chairman and chief executive, he retired from the Houston-area business in 2019. His work centred on improving bank profitability, operations and vendor costs.

long_biography.plain_text:
Floyd began JMFA as a small regional practice with only a handful of employees in Texas. He developed the company around the economics of smaller financial institutions, combining advice on overdraft programs with proprietary compliance software and vendor-contract negotiation.

By the time private-equity firm HKW acquired JMFA, it served more than 350 regional banks and credit unions across the United States. The deal was structured as a majority recapitalisation. Floyd retired alongside Cher Floyd, the firm's co-owner and chief operating officer, leaving a nationwide provider with new leadership and capital for expansion.
